articles.description:
A barcode is not a universal container for whatever text you throw at it. This becomes obvious the first time someone pastes X001ABCDE9 into a UPC-A form and wonders why the form looks unhappy.
UPC-A encodes digits. An Amazon FNSKU contains letters. That is not a formatting preference; it rules out UPC-A and EAN-13 completely.
X001ABCDE9    Amazon FNSKU
B08N5WRWNW    ASIN
036000291452  UPC-A

The first is an FNSKU: a 10-character identifier assigned by Amazon to one seller's offer of one product. The second is an ASIN, the catalog identifier. The third is the manufacturer’s retail barcode. The X00 barcode guide explains why a code beginning with B0 in the FNSKU column usually means the listing is tracked by its manufacturer barcode rather than an Amazon barcode.
For the label itself, FNSKU…
articles.title: Why an Amazon FNSKU Cannot Be a UPC: Code 128 Has Letters

articles.author: Abdeldjalil Chougui
articles.description:
A password manager, a private gallery and an encrypted notes app share one promise: the server stores the data but cannot read it. Keeping that promise takes more than calling an encryption function. You need a way to log in without sending the password. You need to change the password without re-encrypting everything. A record must not be movable to another id. A large file must be encrypted in chunks, and a missing last chunk must be noticed. And you still want to search by email.
Each of these has a known answer, and each is easy to get slightly wrong. e2ee_vault is a small pure Dart toolkit that packages them: an Argon2id key hierarchy, record encryption, a streaming file format that detects truncation, blind indexes, and password tools. It is built on top of package:cryptography.
The …
articles.title: e2ee_vault: a small toolkit for zero-knowledge encrypted vaults in Dart

Last week one endpoint in production started returning 500s. The same code on my laptop worked fine. Same database, same queue, same deploy. The only thing that wasn't the same, as far as I could tell, was configuration.
I pulled the env file off the server (/etc/myapp/.env) and put it next to my local .env.development. 118 lines each. I read them side by side for about forty seconds, and my eyes started gliding. That's the thing about config drift: every line looks boring, and the one broken line looks exactly like the other 117.
So I stopped reading and started diffing. Here are the three ways I now compare config files, from the most manual to the one I reach for first.

Open Code Review is a CLI named ocr. It reads a Git diff, sends changed files to a configurable LLM, and an agent with tool-calling ability produces structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read whole files, search the codebase, and look at other changed files for context. That last part matters: a diff-only reviewer sees a removed line and guesses; an agent that can open the surrounding function sees why the line was there.

articles.description:
Handpic is a culling app for RAW files: you page through what you shot, give stars, reject the rest, and the judgments go into metadata files saved next to the RAW files (XMP or DxO PhotoLab format). It reads only the JPEG previews embedded in the RAW files, never develops anything, and never writes to the RAW files themselves.
It started in September 2026 as a Tauri 2 app (Rust backend, TypeScript UI in WebView2). In November I rewrote the whole UI in GPUI, Zed's GPU-rendered UI framework, and deleted the Tauri app.
Developing apps make you wait every time you move to the next photo. Handpic exists partly to avoid that, so one number matters more than anything else in it: the time from pressing → to the next photo on screen.

Disclosure: I am on the team behind VibUI, a paid prompt library for websites. You will see one mention of it in the last tool section. The accessibility rules here do not depend on it.
Short answer: if you want an AI-built page to pass a basic accessibility check, put the accessibility rules in the first prompt, not in a cleanup message after the layout is finished. Name the contrast target, heading order, form-label behaviour, keyboard focus, image alt rules, landmarks and a prefers-reduced-motion fallback up front. Then run a keyboard pass and an automated scan (Lighthouse or axe) before you call the page done. This applies the same way in v0, Lovable, Bolt, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Replit, GitHub Copilot, Framer AI, Google Stitch, Readdy, Aura.build and OpenAI Codex.
